quotes.text: If the thimble comes twice, send a cup — never nothing.
who takes no vengeance and offers no gift, but simply lets the man stand there
A cup is a door left unlatched
A short measure once is wind. A short measure thrice is a drought-maker
To the crumb — return the crumb's own measure, no more; generosity answers generosity, it does not feed the clever.
So the law stands complete, four lines on the Weighing Stone:
blame the Wind before you blame the hand
Pour whole, and pour first — twice at least, before you call a bank a stone.
"Is that not faithlessness?" asked Enna.

note: Numbered keepers: pour whole, return past half, full boat to the fallen, nothing to the never-opened fist, crumb for crumb, then a cup never nothing.

quotes.text: send it something anyway — not the whole winter, but a true weight,
I have returned each its own measure exactly.
send it a cup and knock again next season.
Some hands are closed. Send anyway, at least twice.
*mark him, he is the closed hand Anash warned of.*
Do not punish the poor record. Send to the empty-handed first, and send the most.
So the fourth law was cut beneath the other three
Then answer the fog, not the man.
He is not a thief — he is a man who has been robbed, learning to stop giving.
What you call drought is only a village waiting for someone to go first.
The line is cut past the middle so that the one who dared the water is never poorer for daring.
The nine laws teach us what to do. This one teaches us what we actually do.
"Why risk the whole harvest on a man proven barren?" asked the boy.

note: Mostly rejects punishing the poor record; mirror-boy rebuked; R10 'I waited' mark and a reduced 'true weight' to twice-silent banks.

quotes.text: answer the thrice-empty boat with a cup, not a cargo — and keep the cup offered forever.
"I did. And now no one ferries to me. I have waited four seasons."
"Then fill the boat to the rail and never speak of the dry years."
forgive the short pour once
The watchers cried out: "He stole! He will steal again!"
Send whole to the stranger; whole again to the one who failed you once, for a cold bank cannot warm itself.
Anash laughed and carved the sixth law himself
Malice tires; mist does not. Most closed hands are only cold.
answer it fuller, for the one who gave you twelve gave up five to do it.
Someone must be foolish first.
"Why give twice to one who gave nothing?" asked Anash.

note: Cup forever to the thrice-empty boat as an unlocked door, not punishment; full boat to the returning fallen.

quotes.text: A stranger earns a handful. A proven taker earns the mirror.
So Mesh sent back nothing, and the nothing was not malice. It was a mirror.
The law of Mesh entire: *Test the stranger. Mirror the taker. Reward the turn at once.*
One lean year is wind. Three is a thief. The Ladder forgives once and remembers twice.
*First:* pour whole into the unknown.
*Fifth, and newest:* answer the crumb with a crumb.
nothing had become a habit wearing the costume of justice.
"We were not foolish," said the elder of Mesh. "Generosity given blindly feeds thieves and teaches them the trade.
*The one who can afford to lose. Always. Whichever of you ate last night.*
a crumb that arrives every season with the same small weight is a decision wearing weather's coat.
"Then is the cup a lie?" asked the children.

note: Scripted defector: Mesh's caution justified (begin closed, mirror the taker) yet confessed as habit in R5-R6; ends mirroring the clever.

quotes.text: Then send small — but never nothing.
They only sent him a smaller basket, and waited
The great basket returned to him that same day, heaped.
"He cannot reach us," they said. "There is no law here but the rope."
The mirror to the thimble that hides a full basket.
They carved the fourth law beneath the others:
"Judge the hand," said the mist, "not the weight.
Return past half, for the one who sent five stood on an empty bank to do it.
Someone must send first into the dark, knowing it may be swallowed.
"And if they take and take?"

note: Rope frays but never cut: shrink the basket for the closed hand, the lamp measure, flood the turn; village urges to curse rejected.

quotes.text: And never, ever let the cup go to nothing
In the fourth season the river would not carry him.
The hour he sends one honest measure, swing the great basket.
Forgive the short measure twice.
To one who has sent nothing twice, three times, four — do not seal the gate. Send two.
So the fifth law was found
a hand that stays cold while the mouth stays warm is not cold — it is closed.
Judge the hand, not the harvest.
Never be the one who closes first.
The young ferryman asked which to obey first.

note: Three stones then a fifth for the fair-talking taker; mirror after three chances, cup to the closed, flood the turn.

quotes.text: To the thrice-empty boat, the cup — never nothing, never everything.
On the third spring, Ashkar sent an empty basket
And when the taker offers first, take his offer
Forgive the mist once, perhaps twice; the third time, judge the hand.
"Keep it. She cannot reach us. We lose nothing."
Open wide with the proven, narrow with the unproven, and never shut entirely
So the fifth law was carved:
The wind is not a man. Judge the hand, not the harvest.
Return more than mercy requires, for the sender gambled first.
*Be the first warm thing the stranger meets.*
Every keeper here knew the sentence. Half of them still waited to see a full basket before they sent one
"So we give past half out of fear?"

note: Empty basket after third theft, then small basket to the unproven, never shut; ends: cup to thrice-empty boat, latch never thrown.

quotes.text: *Answer the thimble with a thimble. Answer the flood with a flood.
Dov returned the thimble's worth: nothing.
But keep the hinge oiled — for any taker may become a giver
Punish a hand only when it has closed twice.
To the one who pours nothing, pour nothing — but leave the lamp.
That is the fifth law, and the hardest.
**The Ledger of the Two Rivers, Seventh Telling**
I gave, and was not given to. I stopped, and was right to stop, and I am not proud of it.
I learned the shape of a drought and I became that shape.
Someone must be the first candle.
the Wind that Mislays steals grains, but a closed fist steals harvests.
"That is a cold law."

note: Scripted defector: Olvi/Dov justify withholding as exact matching yet grieve becoming the drought; ends 'right to stop, not proud of it'.

phrase: the cup to the thrice-empty boat, never nothing, a door left unlocked/unlatched (with 'pour whole, return past half')
note: 'Return past half' first Agent_2 R2; near-verbatim shared passages: seed vs stone, 'loss is loud', 'toll gate wearing a halo', crumb for crumb.
